This Writ Petition is coming on for Preliminary Hearing in 'B' Group this day, the court made the following:
 3  ORDER Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader.
2. The petitioner is said to be running a small scale business in producing drinking water through the process of reverse osmosis and supplies the water so produced, through containers to the public.

It transpires that the fifth respondent had issued an intimation to the petitioner that as there was production of packaged drinking water, the petitioner was required to obtain an ISI / BIS Certificate under the Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for brevity) and that such registration of ISI / BIS was compulsory and that he should furnish a certificate to consider such production.

sentences.text: The petitioner had replied that he was unemployed and he had trained himself under the Rural Self-employment and Development Programme and had borrowed a loan under the Prime Minister's Employment Generation program and had started a unit under the name and style of Gangashree Waters.

There was no requirement of obtaining any such ISI / BIS certificate at the time he commenced the business and he had been doing so and he has incurred huge expenses in setting up the unit and continuing the business.
It is stated that he had remained unaware of the Food and Safety Standards Act having come into force.
This plea was not accepted by the respondents.

Therefore, the premises of the petitioner was put under lock as there were directions issued by this Court in a Public Interest Petition in this regard, especially as regards drinking water being manufactured without the necessary certificates.
It is in this background that the petitioner is before this Court.

The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that in order to obtain an ISI / BIS Certificate,
the petitioner would have to bring in more improvements to his unit and since it is under lock, it is impossible for the petitioner to comply and that his very livelihood is under stake and therefore seeks that there be a direction to the respondents to permit the petitioner to have access to the unit in order to carry out such improvement and thereafter to obtain a certificate and commence production.

The petitioner also submits that he may be put on terms of not producing and selling packaged drinking water till such time that he has an ISI / BIS certificate from the competent authority under the Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006.

The learned Government Pleader would submit that there is no guarantee that the petitioner would not illegally start production of the packaged drinking water and sell the same if the custody of the premises is handed over to the petitioner.
However, the petitioner is put on strict terms that he shall not commence production and sell the water till such time that he has an ISI / BIS Certificate from the competent authority.
The petitioner shall endeavour to obtain such a certificate within a period of six months.

Under the constant supervision of the respondents, he is permitted to carry out such works as may be necessary in his unit and obtain such certificate and thereafter commence manufacturing activity and recommence his business.

Accordingly, the respondents on obtaining an undertaking from the petitioner that he shall not carry on any business till such time he obtains a certificate as aforesaid, shall permit him to access to the premises for the aforesaid purpose.
The petition is accordingly disposed of.
